use_when: Teacher needs to classify current size/runtime, utilization, row pressure, physical structure, legalization/DPO stage behavior, displacement, and liveness counters before routing Students to a full mechanism reconstruction.

For Diamond/sourceTopK feature routes, Teacher describes the first-pass mechanism as the Blueprint D+A core chain: fast clean Diamond start, broad full-source per-source top-K exact sourceTopK producer, cumulative native hot-segment handoff, and hot-frontier selected reorder with bounded fallback; many accepts with a tiny surviving hot frontier is a handoff-lifetime failure; exact local closure and heavier critical-frontier consumers are continuation links after the core is live.

summary: Detailed reconstruction roadmap for selected route families. Blueprint D+A is the one-student Diamond warm-up method: keep the fast clean Diamond start, force broad per-source top-K exact global-swap, export cumulative hot segments, and consume them with hot-frontier selected reorder before optional closure/continuation consumers.
use_when: Teacher has selected Blueprint A, B, C, D, or D+A and needs concrete Student guidance, or Student needs source handles, implementation order, counters, and self-diagnosis rules for that route.
avoid_when: Do not broad-read every route. Use only the Teacher-selected blueprint section after current evidence selects a route; do not reconstruct only a guard or the last small patch.
done_criteria: Teacher names the selected blueprint and copies only that roadmap section or generated route insight packet into Student guidance
Student reconstructs the full cumulative producer-handoff-consumer chain instead of implementing only guard, attribution, telemetry, cap widening, or late polish

For Blueprint A, Student consumes already-live sourceTopK/global-swap accepted-node and hot-critical segment state through micro-start, chain, closure, multi-row, and residual-swap links; if sourceTopK counters are absent or tiny and one Student is assigned, route Blueprint D+A instead of standalone A.

For Blueprint B, Student reconstructs source-edge GS, hot reorder, micro-pack, recoverability producer, accepted-window replay/cascade, endpoint/source repair, and optional pair/small-cluster transactions
For Blueprint C, Student reconstructs LEGALM stage3 current-net anchors, target handoff, frontier global/vertical moves, and selected-segment reorder
Student logs route-specific producer, handoff, consumer, exact-score, replay, accepted-gain, rejection, and pass-runtime counters
Student self-diagnoses which roadmap link is live and which missing link blocks final HPWL movement, then makes one strengthened repair or controlled pivot before finalization

For Blueprint D+A, Student must not stop at producer activation; exact sourceTopK/global-swap with full-source traversal, small ranked per-source candidate pools, exact-probe caps, cumulative native hot-segment handoff, and hot-frontier selected-segment reorder with bounded fallback are the first implementation contract; a one/two-segment surviving frontier after many accepts is a handoff-lifetime failure.

For Blueprint D, profiling and applied passes report generated candidates, exact_scored, positive accepts, accepted_delta, rollback/replay failures, hot-segment handoff, and selected-segment reorder consumption.

For large row-rich one-student warm-up, Student starts from diamond and implements the Blueprint D+A core in one chain: broad bounded exact sourceTopK/global-swap, cumulative native hot-segment handoff, and hot-frontier selected reorder; exact local closure, critical-row, critical-net, multi-row, and residual-swap consumers are optional continuation after core evaluation.

For Blueprint A, Student reconstructs the post-DPO critical-frontier stack: native critical-frontier export, micro-start, critical-net chain, exact closure, multi-row residual transaction, and segment-local residual swap; local closure alone is only one consumer link.
For Blueprint D/D+A, the exact producer uses all-cell pass iteration with per-source top-K bounds; a tiny global ranked-source pool is underbuilt and should be diagnosed as weak source enumeration.

For Blueprint D/D+A, sourceTopK must rank per-source candidate rows/anchors by outside-bbox-distance reduction before exact scoring, then rerun the best positive tryMove/trySwap replay; high exact_scored with zero replay attempts or accepts is a producer-quality failure, not a completed chain.

For Blueprint D+A, a modest clean-Diamond legal-HPWL rise is compatible with the route if sourceTopK accepted delta and final HPWL move strongly; do not force a legalizer rewrite before exact-GS/handoff/reorder are proven live.
For Blueprint D/D+A, tryMove is scored before trySwap and swap is only fallback; exact-scoring both move and swap for every candidate is a runtime bug.
